name: Network pipeline
type: design decision (OpenStreetMap to simulation-graph pipeline: tool comparison and minimal custom pipeline)
maintainer: Tools compared: osmnx (Geoff Boeing, MIT); SUMO netconvert (Eclipse Foundation / DLR, EPL-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later); osm2streets (A/B Street, Dustin Carlino and contributors, Apache-2.0). Pipeline itself: our team.
last_activity: Checked 2026-11-11: osmnx 2.1.1 on PyPI; eclipse-sumo and sumolib 1.28.0 on PyPI; osm2streets main branch active in 2025 (last commit 2025-10-02), npm osm2streets-js 0.1.4 (June 2023).
licence: osmnx MIT; SUMO/netconvert EPL-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later; osm2streets and osm2streets-js Apache-2.0. Output data from all three remains under OSM's ODbL 1.0.
language: osmnx: Python >= 3.11 (geopandas >= 1.0.1, networkx, shapely 2, numpy, pandas, requests). netconvert: C++ binary (pip package eclipse-sumo ships it). osm2streets: Rust, with JS/WASM, Python and Java bindings. Proposed custom pipeline: Python offline (osmnx + custom code) emitting JSON consumed by a TypeScript engine.
maintenance_health: osmnx: mature single-maintainer academic project with regular releases (2.x API since 2024 [uncertain exact date]). SUMO: institutional (DLR), regular releases (1.28.0 current). osm2streets: README warns the API is not stable; npm build not republished since 2023, so JS users lag main.
network_import: Concrete comparison. OUTPUT: osmnx -> networkx MultiDiGraph, GraphML, GeoPackage, GeoDataFrames (no lanes model, one edge per directed way segment); netconvert -> SUMO .net.xml (lanes, internal junction lanes, connections, traffic lights), plain XML (nodes/edges/connections), OpenDRIVE, MATSim; osm2streets -> StreetNetwork JSON or GeoJSON (roads with lane specs, intersection polygons, lane and intersection markings). DIVIDED ROADS: osmnx consolidate_intersections(G, tolerance=10, rebuild_graph=True, max_length=None, dead_ends=False, reconnect_edges=True) merges clusters within a buffer radius (tolerance) on a projected graph; with rebuild_graph=True it checks topology so a street junction under an overpass on-ramp junction is not merged; max_length stops long ramps linking clusters. netconvert --junctions.join (join-dist default 10 m) merges junction clusters from parallel carriageways; skipping it causes short internal edges, throughput loss and deadlocks; --junctions.join-exclude fixes bad joins. osm2streets has MergeDualCarriageways (dual_carriageways.rs, many TODOs, not in the default clipped-area list) plus CollapseShortRoads and CollapseDegenerateIntersections, and refuses to collapse intersections between roads on different layers. TURN RESTRICTIONS: netconvert loads type=restriction relations by default (warns when it cannot apply them); osm2streets stores turn_restrictions and via-way restrictions on Road; osmnx does not model turns or restrictions at all [uncertain: not stated explicitly in osmnx docs]. LANES/WIDTH DEFAULTS: netconvert takes lanes and maxspeed from tags, otherwise from typemaps ('set up ad hoc and not yet verified'); --default.lanenumber 1, --default.lanewidth -1 (SUMO default width) [uncertain whether OSM width tag is read; docs list no such option]; --osm.turn-lanes uses turn:lanes (off by default). osm2streets (osm2lanes) derives a lane list from lanes/oneway/cycleway/parking/sidewalk/placement tags; default driving lane 3.0 m (NORMAL_LANE_THICKNESS), sidewalk 1.5 m, shoulder 0.5 m; legal defaults keyed by country code. osmnx keeps raw tags only (useful_tags_way default: access, area, bridge, est_width, highway, junction, landuse, lanes, maxspeed, name, oneway, ref, service, tunnel, width) and after simplify_graph a merged edge may carry lists of values. LEFT-HAND TRAFFIC: netconvert needs --lefthand; osm2streets has driving_side (osm2streets-js override_driving_side), and falls back to GB rules for left-hand if no country code; osmnx is agnostic (no lanes, so nothing to mirror). BRIDGES/LAYERS: in all three, grade separation works only because OSM bridges do not share nodes with roads below; netconvert --osm.layer-elevation FLOAT raises each layer by FLOAT m (heuristic, max-grade 10% default, manual correction may be needed) and --osm.elevation reads ele tags (experimental); osm2streets reads layer into Road.layer for z-ordering only; osmnx keeps bridge and tunnel tags but not layer by default (must add 'layer' to settings.useful_tags_way). LICENCE/INSTALL: osmnx pip/conda pure Python; netconvert pip install eclipse-sumo or system packages, ~100+ MB [uncertain size]; osm2streets cargo build or npm osm2streets-js WASM.
demand_input_formats: The pipeline outputs only the supply side. Demand is a separate JSON keyed to the pipeline's stable IDs: per entry link, flow by vehicle class per 15 min, and per junction approach, turning ratios (from RITES-style turning counts). Keeping OSM way IDs on every link lets a re-import re-attach demand and signal plans.
data_access: Input via Overpass API (corridor clip, JSON with 'out body' for node IDs or 'out geom' for coordinates) or Geofabrik extracts (India southern-zone-latest.osm.pbf, 533 MB). Output: one static network JSON per demo corridor (expected tens to a few hundred KB for a 2-3 km corridor [uncertain]) bundled with the web app. ODbL obligations for that file: (a) it is a Derivative Database that is Publicly Conveyed, so ODbL 4.2 requires the licence/URI and OSM notices to travel with it; (b) 4.4 share-alike - the file itself must be offered under ODbL (our engine code is unaffected); (c) 4.6 - offer recipients the derivative database or the list of changes/method in machine-readable form (shipping the JSON plus the pipeline script satisfies this); (d) OSMF attribution guideline - visible 'OpenStreetMap' credit linked to openstreetmap.org/copyright on the map (corner, splash or collapsible '(i)'), and attribution plus ODbL link inside the data file/README; (e) simulation screenshots and videos are Produced Works needing only the attribution notice (4.3). Keep non-OSM data (BTP signal timings, counts) in separate files so they are not merged into the ODbL database [uncertain: collective-database interpretation].
runs_in_browser_or_server: Offline, at build time, on a developer machine or CI. Only the resulting JSON ships to the browser. osm2streets-js could run in the browser via WASM, but runtime import is not needed for a fixed demo corridor.
wasm_or_streaming_feasibility: Not required. Pre-import offline and serve static JSON. (osm2streets is the only one of the three with a WASM build; netconvert has no WASM build; osmnx is Python.)
api: osmnx: Python functions (graph_from_bbox/graph_from_polygon with custom_filter, simplify_graph, consolidate_intersections, graph_to_gdfs, save_graph_geopackage). netconvert: CLI options plus sumolib Python reader for .net.xml. osm2streets: Rust API and JS binding (StreetNetwork from OSM XML + clip polygon + options -> GeoJSON/JSON). Our output contract: network.json with nodes {id, x, y, z, osm_node_ids}, links {id, from, to, polyline, lanes, width_m, carriageway_width_m, speed_kmh, z_start, z_end, osm_way_ids, class, is_ramp, is_bridge}, connectors {id, from_link, from_lanes, to_link, to_lanes, movement: L/S/R/U, conflicts[]}, junctions {id, node_ids, type: signal|priority|merge|diverge, z, signal_plan_ref}, meta {source, osm_timestamp, licence: ODbL-1.0, attribution}.
performance: Not a runtime concern: Overpass clip plus osmnx for a 2-3 km corridor runs in seconds to a minute; netconvert on a city district takes seconds to minutes [uncertain: no benchmark measured here].
multi_tenancy_model: N/A at runtime: a static network file shared by all users, served from a CDN; per-user scenario edits are stored as diffs (lane counts, signal plans, closures) against the stable link IDs, not as new networks.
build_complexity: Lowest: osmnx (pip install, about 30 lines to fetch, simplify, consolidate and export) but it yields only centre-line topology, so lanes, connectors and z-levels are custom code (est. 4-8 h). Medium: netconvert (one command with recommended options gives lanes and lane-to-lane connections; parsing .net.xml into our JSON is 2-4 h, but it brings SUMO's lane-level geometry and internal junction lanes we may not want). Highest risk: osm2streets (best lane geometry, but unstable API, stale npm package, dual-carriageway merge experimental, would add Rust/WASM toolchain). Recommended hybrid within 72 hours: Overpass -> osmnx (with layer added to useful tags) -> custom lane/connector/z builder -> JSON, and run netconvert once on the same clip as a cross-check of lane connections and joined junctions.
scenario_editability: Pipeline should make these editable downstream by keeping stable IDs: lane count and width per link, ramp open/closed, connector permissions (turn bans), signal plan per junction, link closure/lane blockage. Geometry edits (new flyover) are out of scope in 72 h; pre-build alternative networks offline instead.
output_metrics_supported: N/A for the pipeline; it must emit detector locations (link id + offset) at junction stop lines and flyover landings so the engine can report queues and GEH against counts.
known_limitations: OSM input quality dominates: in Bengaluru, width is tagged on about 1% of major-road length and lanes on about 48% (and on 407 of 617 major bridge ways), turn:lanes is effectively absent, so every tool falls back to defaults or guesses lane connections. netconvert typemaps are self-described as unverified; netconvert lane defaults (1 lane) are wrong for Indian arterials without a typemap tuned for India. osmnx consolidation is purely geometric within tolerance even with rebuild_graph topology checks; it does not use layer, and simplified edges can carry list-valued lanes/width that need a reduction rule. osm2streets geometry is explicitly weak near bridges/tunnels and on-off ramps ('Incorrect near bridges/tunnels'), and its dual-carriageway merge is experimental. None of the tools validates bridge topology: a bridge that wrongly shares a node with a ground road silently creates an at-grade junction.
documented_failures: SUMO docs: OSM imports without --junctions.join create short internal edges that cause throughput loss, jams and deadlocks; restriction relations crossing the clip boundary are ignored with warnings. A/B Street (osm2streets lineage): one broken bridge in Seattle spread gridlock across the map, and short roads and ramps remained an unsolved geometry problem. osmnx examples notebook: naive geometric consolidation (rebuild_graph=False) would merge a street junction with the on-ramp junction of the overpass above it - the motivating case for topology-aware consolidation.
validation_approach: Pipeline acceptance checks to implement: (1) z-consistency - every node shared by two links must have equal z on both; any link with bridge=yes must have z>=1 (layer default 1) and no interior node shared with a z=0 link (an Overpass check on Bengaluru found 0 such cases among major roads today, so the check is cheap insurance); (2) flag layer>0 without bridge and layer<0 without tunnel (55 and 39 cases citywide); (3) strong connectivity of the drivable graph from every source to every sink (networkx strongly_connected_components), with dangling one-way stubs listed; (4) every connector's from-lanes and to-lanes within lane counts and every junction has at least one outgoing connector per incoming lane; (5) lane-sum sanity: lanes x width <= carriageway width when width is known; (6) diff against a netconvert run on the same clip (number of joined junctions, connections per junction); (7) visual overlay on imagery for the demo corridor.
takeaway_for_our_build: Do not import OSM at runtime and do not trust any tool's defaults. Build an offline, deterministic pipeline: Overpass clip (keep node IDs) -> osmnx graph with 'layer', 'turn:lanes', 'lanes:forward/backward', 'bridge', 'tunnel' added to useful_tags_way -> simplify_graph with edge_attrs_differ=['lanes','layer','bridge','oneway'] so lane-count and grade changes split links -> consolidate_intersections(rebuild_graph=True, tolerance about 10-15 m, max_length set so ramps are not used to link clusters) applied only to z=0 nodes, with z>0 nodes excluded from the tolerance dict -> custom builder that assigns z from layer (bridge without layer -> 1), fills lanes/width from an India class table (trunk 3 x 3.5 m per direction, primary 2 x 3.5 m, links 1-2 x 3.5 m, at-grade 3.0 m per the Hebbal DPR) overridden by a hand-edited patch file keyed by OSM way ID, generates connectors by lane-index matching with left-hand rules (keep-left, right turns from the rightmost lanes), and applies turn restrictions from relations -> run the acceptance checks -> emit network.json with ODbL metadata. Cross-check once with netconvert --lefthand --junctions.join --osm.layer-elevation 6, and keep osm2streets only as an optional visual reference for intersection polygons.
